label: text
text: INTEREST THAT RISES.

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Singapore, October 5:

label: text
text: At the urgent request of the Secretary of State, the Government has agreed that the Colony should advance the Hongkong Government sums not exceeding one million pounds, these advances to come out of the currency guarantee fund.

label: text
text: Upon enquiry locally the “China Mail” was informed that owing to the delay which would be involved, it had not been anticipated that the loan would be raised on the London market, and some Colonies had signified willingness to co-operate in providing the money. Such Colonies, in common with Hongkong, conducted the negotiations for the employment of their reserves through the Crown agents and such a loan as that to Hongkong would provide suitable employment.

label: text
text: It can be readily understood that a loan for a short period with suitable interest would serve the interests of such Colonies much better than a long term loan and it is understood that the Hongkong Government looks upon the loan to them as a short one, in fact the interest to be charged them will be on a rising scale so it is obvious that local borrowers will be expected to pay back bbrrowed sums comparatively soon.

label: paragraph_title
text: MOTORS COLLIDE.

label: text
text: DRIVERS' CONFLICTING VERSIONS.

label: text
text: ROBINSON ROAD REPAIRS

label: text
text: The repairs which are being effected to Robinson Road were indirectly the cause of an accident which had a court sequel this morning.

label: text
text: The owners of two motor cars which collided at the junction of Robinson Road with Mosque Street were plaintiff and defendant respectively, the former being Noor Ahmed of the Wanchai garage and the latter, Leung Yuen-cheung.

label: text
text: The plaintiff's driver claimed that the defendant's driver drove on the part of the road which was not being repaired at a speed of 20 miles an hour and gave plaintiff, who was turning the corner, no chance of avoiding him. The plaintiff had the right of way on that portion of the road.

label: text
text: The defendant said that he was going at 10 miles an hour. He turned into the portion of the road which was up when he saw the other car coming and at the time of the collision was stationary. He did not hear plaintiff sound a horn.

label: text
text: Cross-examined by Mr. H. S. Fitzroy, who appeared for the plaintiff, defendant admitted that the portion of the road which was not up was not much wider than the width of his car. There was a big hole where the road was up. He denied that he had admitted that he was in the wrong by asking the other driver to get repairs effected and charge him (defendant) with them.

label: text
text: His Honour found that defendant had been guilty of dangerous driving and dismissed the counterclaim which he had brought forward. His Honour also adjourned the matter of damages. (Plaintiff claimed $463 for actual damages and loss of use of car).

label: paragraph_title
text: THIRD COUP.

label: text
text: CANTON RED'S LATEST MOVE.

label: text
text: GENERAL DETAINED?

label: text
text: Yet another coup—the third of the present régime—has been brought off by General Cheung Kai-shek, the commander of the Canton Cadets. This coup has resulted in the disarming of several hundreds of non-Cantonese mercenaries in Canton, the rounding-up of about sixty officials and the reported detention of General Hung Hak-mu of Szechuan.

label: text
text: The net result is the further strengthening of the hands of the Cadet commandant. General Hung has a strength estimated at 10,000 bayonets on the North River, and the morale of his rank and file is bound to be badly shaken.

label: text
text: It was only a few weeks ago that General Hung, together with another non-Cantonese adventurer, brought his following into Canton province. Inspired reports from Canton hinted that he was welcomed by General Cheung who had a view to a non-Cantonese alliance to overcome the Cantonese armies should they ever become united.

label: text
text: General Hung once held a command in his native province. In the earlier days of the Republic he was an ardent admirer of Choy Ngok (Chai Yo) who died after inflicting the first check on Yuan Shi-kai's monarchical plans. Hung is said to be allied to Tuchun Tang Chi-yao of Yunnan.

label: text
text: was ordered to attend the headquarters of the Kuomintang Government to answer a charge of moving his troops without orders. There he was ordered to be detained by General Cheung, says the report. Simultaneously, his army headquarters in Canton city was surrounded by a detachment of Cadets who immediately disarmed the bodyguards. Military pickets were also sent out to search the residence of Hung's higher officers.

label: text
text: A later message to the "Wah Tsz Yat Po" suggests that an armed force is being sent to the North River to bring about the capitulation of General Hung's main force.

label: text
text: Yesterday there was a rumour in town concerning a Red coup in Canton but it could not be confirmed.

label: text
text: The Russian officer who has been appointed as admiral of the Canton Navy is reported to be contemplating early resignation on account of financial trouble.

label: text
text: It was expected, says the "Wah Tsz Yat Po" that $500,000 would be paid for refitting the Canton Navy when the appointment was made. Keen disappointment is felt at non-payment. The admiral is believed to be asking, shortly, for leave to return to Russia, where he will then hand in his resignation to Canton.

text: REGISTRATION PROBLEM.

label: text
text: A local Chinese firm has approached the “China Mail” regarding a certain amount of delay entailed in the receipt and despatch of registered letters from Hongkong, which delay in important messages they consider it is in the general interests to try to imitate us far no possible.

label: text
text: The position with regard to the receipt of registered letters is that delivery is made in the case of Euro-seem firms and private individuals but in the case of Chinese identity being very difficult to establish, receivers have to send a representative to the Chinese branch at the general Post Office where they have to produce the chop of the particular firm, or in the case of in

label: text
text: A “China Mail” representative who made enquiries at the Post Office this morning was assured that this was the only reliable means of assuring that the letter was received by the proper persons. The number of postmen employed was now almost back to normal, but a number of the men were now and the despatch of registered letters by them was not considered a wise policy. It was purely in the interests of the receivers that the pre

label: text
text: With regard to a suggestion made by the firm which approached the "China Mail" that there should be appointed as receivers of registered letters certain well-known firms in each district and that this would correspondingly decrease the delay in going through so many letters at the General Post Office, it was pointed out to the "China Mail" representative that the Post Office was responsible for seeing that the letters reached their destination and was liable if anything went wrong. It would be impossible to delegate these powers, and there were also other formalities involved which required a certain amount of organisation.

label: text
text: With regard to outgoing registered letters, any delay was due to the very much increased number of letters being registered in consequence of troubled conditions in China. text: “SUI YIK” SCENES.

label: text
text: DISARMED TROOPS SENT TO CANTON.

label: text
text: MORE ARMS SEIZED.

label: text
text: The large number of Cantonese troops from the s.s. "Sui Yik" were safely placed over the border on Thursday. The Chinese authorities at Shumchun later conveyed the soldiers to Canton by train.

label: text
text: Prior to the men being placed on the train at Kowloon, they were again searched and several loaded revolvers were found on them. The weapons had apparently been secreted on the vessel and the attempt to take them away proved unsuccessful.

label: text
text: The vessel was handed back to her local owners, the Fuk Hoi Company, but not before a thorough search had again been made when 30,000 rounds of ammunition in addition to the seizures already made were found concealed in unlikely places on the boat.

label: paragraph_title
text: JUDICIAL INQUIRY.

label: text
text: BOYCOTT BY SHANGHAI CHINESE.

label: text
text: CHAMBER OF COMMERCE FIẾT.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Shanghai, October 6.

label: text
text: The Shanghai Chinese General Chamber of Commerce, in a full page advertisement in the foreign newspapers, declares that all Chinese citizens will under no circumstances be identified or associated with the judicial inquiry.

label: text
text: The Waichiaopu in a Note to the Senior Minister given out this evening and dated October 2, states that the Chinese Government informed the British Charge d'Affaires on September 1, that judicial enquiry into the Shanghai incident would only further complicate the issue and involve a waste of time, and the Chinese Government does not waver from this attitude.

label: text
text: The Note reiterates the view that the lapse of time has changed the circumstances. Most the requisite evidence has become un-obtainable or, has disappeared.

label: text
text: The Note states that after the Shanghai incident and the Chinese Government's protest the Powers sent diplomatic representatives to Shanghai and these representatives i.e. vestigated the case.

label: text
text: though negotiations were brought into suspense through the diplomatic representatives' lack of authority to settle the case, yet no question arose in respect of the facts.

label: text
text: Afterwards when the British Government proposed a re-investigation by judicial procedure, the Chinese Government instructed the Charge d'Affaires in London to inform the British Government that re-investigation was unnecessary. This view was also made known on several occasions to the representatives of the interested Powers.

label: text
text: The Chinese Government did not waver from the attitude originally maintained.

label: text
text: The British steamer "Laomedon" from Yokohama and Penang to New York, which left Colombo on September 29, reports that she lost her propeller in latitude 10/10 North longitude. 61/42 East, owing to a fracture in the tail end of the shaft.

label: text
text:
The steamer "Myrmidon" will tow the boat to Aden or Perim.
[Both the "Laomedon" (6,692 tons) and the "Myrmidon" (4,964 tons) are in the China Mutual Steam Navigation Co.'s fleet (Blue Funnel Line), for which Messrs. Butterfield and Swire are agents there.]
